confirmed: Criterion 3 holds for all five outcomes. Trained undergraduate coders, blind to condition, rated every idea 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) on originality, feasibility, and fun, and each participant's score is the mean over that participant's ideas. Quantity is the number of unique ideas typed in the Word document, and flexibility is the number of distinct categories (of 13) in each participant's list. None is a self-report (PDF p. 5, Section 4.4).

AI availability and question hold. The AI-assisted arms used Microsoft Co-pilot during the 10-minute ideation phase in which the scored ideas were typed, and the independent arms brainstormed alone. The anticipated teammate belongs to a later, potential group session. So ai_available_when_produced is yes and question is with_ai for all five outcomes (PDF p. 4, Section 4.2; p. 5, Sections 4.2-4.3; p. 9, Fig. 1).

No across_people or after_ai outcome exists. No outcome compares different participants' ideas, and the paper reports no outcome from the anticipated group session ('Potential Group Interaction') or from any later unassisted task (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 4.4 and 5.1-5.4; p. 9, Fig. 1).

Constructs hold. Originality ('the novelty and uniqueness of the idea') is novelty, feasibility ('the ease of implementation') is usefulness, quantity is fluency, and fun ('perceived enjoyability') is other, as for c006 'Enjoyable' and c168 'funny'. Flexibility counts categories within one participant's list, so it is flexibility, not diversity, although the paper calls it 'the diversity of their idea pool' (PDF p. 3, Section 2.3; p. 5, Section 4.4).

Measures hold. Student coders are human_raters, as for the student raters in c035 and c167, and quantity and flexibility are hand counts, so category_count. The ICCs in measure_detail match: .76/.70/.71 with four coders on about 16 percent of ideas, and .84/.78/.75 with two coders on about 20 percent. An addition, not an error: the remaining ideas were split among coders and rated by one coder each (PDF p. 5, Section 4.4).

Unit participant holds. Quality scores are per-participant means, flexibility is a per-participant count, and every main-effect test has error df 208 (212 minus 4). The simple effects have df 135 (137 minus 2) and 73 (75 minus 2), one row per participant within each teammate group (PDF p. 5, Section 4.4; pp. 6-7, Sections 5.2-5.4).

The pooled contrasts match exactly. Table 1 independent vs AI-assisted means (SD) are 13.24 (5.8) vs 11.69 (7.00), 2.99 (.47) vs 3.34 (.56), 3.43 (.56) vs 3.37 (.70), 3.18 (.56) vs 3.44 (.73), and 6.66 (1.95) vs 6.06 (2.22). The main-effect and interaction F, η², and p values for all five outcomes match the text (PDF p. 9, Table 1, read on the page image; pp. 6-7, Sections 5.2-5.4).

Cell ns 69, 68, 37, and 38 sum to 212, so 106 per ideation condition. All eleven direction codes follow the printed means and p-values. The statistics_available tags fit: per-cell analyzed ns are printed, each contrast has a 1-df F test, and CIs exist only for the three tagged simple effects (PDF p. 4, Section 4; p. 6, Section 5.3).

The internal arithmetic is consistent. Cell-size-weighted averages of the Section 5.3 cell means reproduce the Table 1 marginal means within rounding. Every η² equals F/(F + error df), so the printed η² are partial. Each CI is centered on its cell difference (.50, −.44, .455) (computed from PDF p. 6, Section 5.3 and p. 9, Table 1).

Open question 4 can be answered from the printed numbers. With the pooled within-cell variance from the Section 5.3 SDs, tests of the unweighted marginal means give F of about 16.96 (originality), 2.85 (feasibility), and 4.22 (fun), against printed 16.78, 2.71, and 4.23. Tests of the weighted Table 1 means give about 26.2, 0.61, and 9.28. So the printed F tests compare unweighted means (SPSS Type III), while Table 1 prints weighted means. The 'reported' strings record both as printed, and no direction changes (computed from PDF p. 6, Section 5.3 and p. 9, Table 1).

S1-O4 measure_detail ('The paper does not say who counted them') holds for Section 4.4. Section 4.5 says only that responses were 'coded to generate quantitative indicators' and that 'Trained coders evaluated all responses', which implies but does not state who counted (PDF p. 5, Section 4.4; p. 6, Section 4.5).

primary not_stated holds. Preregistered Hypothesis 1 covers quantity, quality, and flexibility together, the paper names no primary outcome, and it calls the interaction follow-ups exploratory (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 4, Hypotheses 3a-3b; p. 6, Section 5.3).

No outcome is missing. Besides the five, the paper reports only impression management, a self-reported five-item scale used as a manipulation check. The post-study motivation measures are not reported. The anticipated-teammate main effects do not vary AI, and arrival set that factor (PDF p. 5, Sections 4.2 and 4.4; p. 6, Section 5.1; p. 9, Table 1).
summary: All five outcomes (originality, feasibility, and fun rated per idea by trained undergraduate coders blind to condition, plus the count of unique ideas and the count of idea categories) are scored on the ideas participants typed, with Co-pilot available in the AI arms, so criterion 3 holds and with_ai is the right question for each. Construct, measure, unit, AI availability, directions, and every number in the eleven contrasts match the PDF (Table 1 read on the page image), and no outcome that bears on the three questions is missing.
